newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil slips, barges jammed by Nov IPE duel.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil slips, barges jammed by Nov IPE duel.

text.p: A dispute between two major European trading houses over the Nov IPE gas oil contract again slowed physical trade on Thursday, with barge premiums slightly easier and those for cargoes unchanged, traders said.
Benchmark Dec IPE futures slid $4.75 to $219 a tonne, reversing gains of $2 on Wednesday. Barge premiums were slightly softer but cargo premiums were discussed unchanged.
Traders said the play, involving over 600,000 tonnes, soaked up most barge capacity in the Rotterdam region.
"It's crazy. The big problem is that in the whole of the Amsterdam area we have to wait three days to load," one said.

Trading house AIC, the dominant Nov short, said it appeared Cargill, the main long, had not been able to take full delivery in the first of three five-day delivery periods. Cargill said there were some problems but hoped to resolve these.
Heating oil barges traded at Dec IPE $2 and +$1.75 fob ARA with storage material done at Dec IPE +$1.50. One low suplhur barge was done at Dec +$13 with another at +$12 basis Flushing.
A cargo of low sulphur diesel with wax additive was traded at Dec IPE +$17 into Rostock, around unchanged. Cargoes of heating oil refinery grade were discussed around Dec IPE +$5/6.
